title: Sr. Director, Global Manufacturing Strategy & Network Transformation
text:
Location:
Buffalo, NY, US, 14213

Req ID: 41812

Segment: Supply Chain

Rich’s, also known as Rich Products Corporation, is a family-owned food company dedicated to inspiring possibilities. From cakes and icings to pizza, appetizers and specialty toppings, our products are used in homes, restaurants and bakeries around the world. Beyond great food, our customers also gain insights to help them stay competitive, no matter their size. Our portfolio includes creative solutions geared at helping food industry professionals compete in foodservice, retail, in-store bakery, deli, and prepared foods, among others. With more than 13,500 associates working globally in 100 countries and annual sales of $5.9 billion, Rich’s is a global leader with a focus on everything that family makes possible. Rich’s®—Infinite Possibilities. One Family.

**Purpose Statement**
---------------------

The Senior Director/VP, Global Manufacturing Strategy & Network Transformation will shape and drive the long-term manufacturing strategy for the enterprise, with primary accountability for the global TCCS manufacturing network and a broader mandate to identify opportunities across the total manufacturing enterprise. Reporting to the Head of Operations, this leader will guide critical decisions around manufacturing footprint, capacity and capability, capital deployment, technology, and operating standards across businesses and regions.

This role will be instrumental in ensuring the manufacturing network is positioned to support significant global growth and evolving business needs. The leader will take an enterprise-wide view of manufacturing, connecting sites, regions, and businesses to optimize existing assets and capabilities, identify network opportunities, anticipate future capacity requirements, and inform strategic investments.

Working across regional and business manufacturing organizations, Supply Chain, Quality, R&D, Finance, Procurement, and Commercial, this executive will bring together complex operational and business inputs to establish clear manufacturing priorities and translate strategy into an actionable, long-range network roadmap. The role will also serve as a trusted manufacturing advisor to the Head of Operations and broader executive leadership team.

**Key Accountabilities and Outcomes**
-------------------------------------

* Set the long-term vision and network roadmap for global TCCS manufacturing, aligned to the Enterprise TCCS strategic plan and Vision 2030, and help shape the broader enterprise manufacturing strategy.
* Act as the manufacturing business partner to the EBU lead: bring manufacturing input into the annual strategic planning cycle, flag where growth plans require new lines or capabilities, and coordinate regional responses through one point of contact.
* Partner with Supply Chain Planning to model capacity against growth plans over a five-year horizon, identifying where and when the network will run short and recommending the best response: add lines, build new capacity, use open capacity in another region, or consolidate.
* Lead network optimization and footprint scenarios across regions, such as building new capacity in one country versus using available capacity in another, or rebalancing frozen and aseptic/UHT capacity, recognizing that idle capacity also carries cost.
* Partner with Finance on major capacity and capability investments, including greenfield and brownfield projects: bring the operational view to the business case, test assumptions on cost, capacity, risk, and timing, and help shape recommendations for executive approval.
* Prepare the network for strategic global customers and programs by anticipating long-lead equipment needs, including when to pre-purchase or hold critical equipment so growth is not delayed by equipment lead times.
* Set equipment strategy across sites, including where to standardize equipment and line design (for example, common aerators and processing equipment), and define required certifications, specifications, and hygienic design standards.
* Partner with Procurement on equipment sourcing, including qualifying new and lower-cost vendors and using economies of scale when several lines are installed in different regions at the same time.
* Support the capital planning process, led by Finance, by working with plants and regional leaders to build the right capital requests, grounded in growth plans, equipment age and life cycle, and historical spend, so capital goes where it creates the most value.
* Design a global critical spare parts strategy, including hub- or region-based stocking of high-value parts such as homogenizer blocks, to lower cost while protecting uptime.
* Use manufacturing KPIs across the TCCS network (yield, OEE, cost, uptime, and resource use such as water per liter produced) to benchmark sites, spot gaps, and identify the biggest opportunities to optimize performance and cost.
* Turn those opportunities into results by working with program and functional leaders, including TPM, Smart Factory, Engineering, Quality, Procurement, and the regional manufacturing teams, to prioritize, launch, and track improvement initiatives, capture gains before adding capacity, and scale proven practices across the network.
* Support high-priority global customer launches by coordinating across regions when issues arise, such as shifting production to another site or country.
* Partner with regional manufacturing leaders as a peer and strategic advisor: align on network priorities, co-develop multi-year regional roadmaps, and support delivery through clear governance, milestones, decision gates, and measurable outcomes.
* Build organizational capability in manufacturing strategy, network optimization, and capital planning across the TCCS network, and lead a small, high-impact team that supports the regions.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Experience**
-------------------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Business, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, manufacturing, operations, or engineering, including at least 5 years at the Director level or above with multi-site and multi-country responsibility.
* Experience across more than one supply chain discipline, such as manufacturing operations, engineering, network design and optimization, capacity planning, S&OP, or supply chain finance. Candidates from finance or strategy roles with significant supply chain exposure are encouraged to apply.
* Track record leading or shaping network and footprint decisions across multiple sites or countries, such as capacity expansion, consolidation, site selection, or make-versus-buy and inter-plant sourcing.
* Experience partnering with Finance to build business cases for capital investments (new lines, plant expansions, greenfield or brownfield projects) and supporting them through approval and execution.
* Food or beverage manufacturing experience preferred; experience with aseptic, UHT, frozen, or dairy processing is a plus.
* Exposure to manufacturing performance and asset programs such as TPM, OEE and yield improvement, lean, critical spares and equipment life-cycle management, equipment standardization and sourcing, or digital and Smart Factory initiatives.
* Experience working in a global, matrixed organization with teams across regions and time zones (for example, Asia, Europe, and Latin America). Fluency in English required; additional languages a plus.

**Attributes for Success**

* Influences without authority: has delivered results through plant and regional leaders who did not report to them, by building trust, negotiating, and showing others what is in it for them.
* Analytical and data-driven: comfortable working with operational and financial data, knows which questions to ask, and turns analysis into clear, practical recommendations.
* Learns fast and drives results: a self-starter who gets up to speed quickly on new businesses, technologies, and regions, and can build a new role and strategy with minimal direction.
* Clear communicator, humble, and collaborative: communicates well up and down the organization and across cultures, follows up in writing, readily shares credit, and adapts their style to different audiences.

**Location, Travel, and Work Schedule**

* Location is flexible; Buffalo, NY is preferred given close partnership with the Head of Operations and headquarters leadership.
* Travel of approximately 30%, mainly in the first year to learn the regions and build relationships with teams and sites in Asia, Latin America, and the US; ongoing travel based on business needs, not constant travel.
* As a global role, flexibility for early-morning or evening meetings with teams in Asia, Europe, and Latin America is required.
